images.title: Add 6, end on 3
images.purpose: Shows that changing the added number from 4 to 6 makes the trick always end on 3.
images.composition: One horizontal chain of four rounded boxes joined by three labelled arrows.
images.exact_structure: Four rounded rectangular boxes in one row, white fill, dark outline, joined left to right by three arrows. Box 1 holds x. Box 2 holds 2x + 6, with the 6 drawn in reddish purple #CC79A7. Box 3 holds x + 3, with the 3 in reddish purple #CC79A7. Box 4 is larger, filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with a white 3. Above the arrows, in order, in teal #0072B2: × 2, + 6 on the first arrow (one label), ÷ 2 on the second, − x on the third. Nothing else is drawn. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, which is large and centred; no scenery, no people, no other text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: The number you add, halved, is the number you end on.
images.description: Shows that changing the added number from 4 to 6 makes the trick always end on 3.
images.context: Picture for changing a step of the Think of a Number trick.
images.teaching_notes: Point at the two purple marks: 6 halves to 3. Then ask what to add for a final 5.

image_decisions.why: Colouring the 6 and the 3 alike shows which step decides the answer, which a line of text hides.
